ballots.fatal_flaw: The fixture-only amendment fence covers only gate-core semantics, while the migration simultaneously moves the majority of attackable surface (the network-boundary evidence collector, ~40 hand-modeled evidence.json files, the runner) OUTSIDE that fence and INTO PR #444 — the exact PR the sprint-4 plan ordered frozen and shrunk because reviewing it manufactures ~100 issues/day. The loop the panel exists to stop is not ended; it is re-hosted on a strictly larger artifact, and merge (hence any release) recedes.
ballots.attack_trace: Sequence: (1) Per migration step 2 and accepted risk 5, #444 grows from docs-only to the full M4 implementation: paginated GraphQL collector, old-file-coordinate hunk parser, three-way signature identity resolution, ~40 hand-authored evidence fixtures, all under the 95% coverage floor. The factory's own throughput record says this stalls: sprint-3 committed core closed 0/5 items in a full sprint, PR #318 sat 3 sprints with zero delta (#978), and #444 itself has been re-reviewed 20 times without reaching mergeable. Every additional week #444 stays open is another week of the 2.6x manufacture loop (PRODUCT.md headline, #980). (2) The 'finding = failing fixture' protocol only binds findings against gate-core's decide() semantics. Findings against collector fidelity ('this evidence.json mis-models real paginated GraphQL', pagination edges, signature-object shape) are BY THE PROPOSAL'S OWN SEAM not expressible as gate-core fixtures — and its own biggestRisk field concedes the collector is 'where a hostile reviewer should aim.' (3) Those findings route through the ordinary review->tech-debt law via the de-dup clerk that is still broken (#471/#688 — never mentioned once in this proposal), which re-files duplicates on every /review and self-blocks the debt-reconcile Stop hook. Round 27+ therefore reviews a larger surface with the manufacture engine untouched. Net product outcome: spec convergence is solved, but v1.0.0 gets FARTHER away this sprint, which is the precise failure mode (#980) the panel convened to stop.
ballots.evidence_basis: Proposal's own biggestRisk ('a hostile reviewer will correctly say the god-spec didn't disappear — part of it moved into a bash script at the network boundary') and risks_accepted[4] ('bigger PR'); PRODUCT.md sprint-4 headline (#980: 289->754 in 6 days, ~100/day against #444's rounds); #471/#688 absent from the proposal; sprint-3 record of 0/5 committed-core closes.
ballots.fix_direction: Phase the migration: merge the ~20-line spec + amendment-protocol text docs-only FIRST (one round, freeze holds), then land gate-core+fixtures and the collector as separate small PRs already governed by the new fixture-only admissibility rule, with #471/#688 as named prerequisites of resuming any adversarial review.

ballots.fatal_flaw: Internal contradiction that permanently deadlocks the first release: design rule 2 says a ledger row that fails its mechanical bindings 'BLOCKS and cannot be signed into exemption — never an override', while migration step 4 promises the ~465 design-superseded review-loop findings will be 'closed... witnessed in one signed ack.' Both cannot be true. Under the proposal's own text the manufactured backlog has no legal disposal path, so the gate returns FAIL on every release attempt forever — and even absent the backlog, every future release of a factory whose entire job is closing findings requires a bus-factor-1 human signature, converting the lights-out factory to human-cadence permanently.
ballots.attack_trace: Sequence: (1) Synthesis merges; first /ship runs the gate; the ledger enumerates every gate-relevant close since 2026-07-29, including the ~465 findings filed against superseded spec drafts. (2) Bindings are hard per-row preconditions no signature can override: a finding against now-deleted prose has no merged change whose default-branch squash message cites its fingerprint AND whose diff hunks overlap its location — meta-findings like #940/#911/#963 (PRODUCT.md names them as self-referential to #444's contested claims) have no code location at all, and prose locations fail the anchored grammar fail-closed pending #649's agent-run normalization, which the proposal itself flags as corruptible. (3) Those rows BLOCK; the only textual cures are a #894 remediation commit (impossible — there is nothing to fix; the 'defect' was prose that no longer exists) or reopening — which throws them back into fail-closed triage and the floored open-issue criteria, where they are un-closable for the identical reason. Deadlock. (4) Steady state is no better: the ledger is non-empty whenever ANY gate-relevant issue closed since baseline — i.e., always, in a factory that closes tech-debt for a living — so every release blocks on the single human whom GOVERNANCE.md models as interacting 'through issues and PRs like anyone else' plus kill switches, and whom the repo's own memory records as 'human only for setup-only acts.' Risk 1 accepts this 'deliberately,' but accepting a flaw openly does not make the gate go green: this proposal ships v1.0.0 never.
ballots.evidence_basis: Traceable contradiction between proposal design[1] ('cannot be signed into exemption ... never an override') and migration[3]/step 4 ('witnessed in one signed ack'); PRODUCT.md #980 record establishes the ~465 findings exist and are largely artifacts of superseded drafts; GOVERNANCE.md 'Humans' section for the operator model.
ballots.fix_direction: Add exactly one explicitly-witnessed disposal class — ADR-referenced 'design-superseded' close, human-signed with per-row provenance in the ledger — or route the manufactured findings to open-P2/P3 triage (open non-floored P2/P3 does not block) instead of pretending they can pass fix-bindings; keep the roster chain-of-custody criterion, which is genuinely valuable and cheap.

ballots.fatal_flaw: The nightly repair auditor's heuristics pivot on an undefined predicate — heuristic (c) reopens duplicate-closes whose target is not 'open-and-gate-relevant or legitimately closed', but 'legitimately closed' is exactly the close-laundering definition this proposal just deleted (demoted to advisory annotations). The auditor must therefore fail-open (no anti-laundering at all, gate purpose unmet) or fail-closed (mass false reopens of genuinely fixed work during the very burn-down the release requires), and the fail-closed horn re-inflates the blocking criteria nightly while flooding the one human signature with a contested-closes blob — the per-exemption burden dx-first mocked, relocated to release-eve and made unreviewable.
ballots.attack_trace: Sequence, fail-closed horn: (1) Getting from 754 open tech-debt to zero means thousands of gate-relevant closes between the 2026-07-29 baseline and the release attempt; the auditor scans every one nightly. (2) #420 merges and closes with its fix PR; its recorded duplicate family (#328/#419/#610/#698/#864/#977, per PRODUCT.md) chains to a now-CLOSED target; the auditor has no executable definition of 'legitimately closed' (the bindings that would decide it are advisory report content by design bullet 5), so a conservative reading reopens all six with needs-triage comments — criterion 4 (fail-closed triage) goes red overnight on already-fixed work. Repeat category-wide across the dedup-heavy backlog (broken de-dup #471/#688 means duplicate-close is THE dominant disposal verb) and the gate's zero-counts become a nightly-receding target: false-red the morning of every release attempt. (3) Each re-close of a falsely-reopened issue lands permanently in 'contested closes'; the release report the single human must sign accretes hundreds of rows with no per-row resolution mechanism defined, so the lone control left standing (one signature, since ALL bindings are advisory) is either a rubber stamp over a blob or an indefinite release block on one absent human. Fail-open horn: if the auditor instead treats closed targets as legitimate, close-the-duplicate-target is an invisible laundering lane and the 'self-healing' claim is void. Bonus, traceable collision: the migration's own mass-close of the ~two-dozen spec-machinery findings 'referencing the synthesis ADR' has no merged closing PR and no default-branch commit naming each issue, so heuristic (b) reopens the proposal's own migration on night one.
ballots.evidence_basis: Undefined 'legitimately closed' in design[2] heuristic (c) versus design[5] demoting all binding logic to advisory; heuristic (b) text versus migration step 3's ADR-referenced mass-close; PRODUCT.md's named duplicate family and #471/#688 showing duplicate-closes will dominate the burn-down.
ballots.fix_direction: Define close-legitimacy as a small pure predicate with fixtures (contract-first's gate-core discipline applied to the auditor, not the gate), and record ADR-referenced disposal closes in an on-disk allowlist the report displays, so the auditor never reopens a close the synthesis itself authorized.
